_about: Hand-maintained list of papers DiaGrad builds on. Everything else (authors, versions, dates, license, hashes) is fetched by tools/build_provenance.py. 'why' notes were drafted from each paper's abstract on 2026-09-24 and are not yet reviewed; reviewed=true marks checked entries. Entries with a 'proceedings' block instead of 'arxiv' are non-arXiv papers: metadata from the publisher's BibTeX, cross-checked with OpenAlex (build_provenance.py --proceedings-only refreshes just these).

papers.why: Engram: hashed N-gram lookup memory as a sparsity axis complementary to MoE; U-shaped allocation law between MoE compute and static memory. The Engram half of CAMOE builds directly on this.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: confirms Engram is built in (196B params, 2 modules at layers 1 and 14). Its Causal Encoder-Decoder splits the stack into encoder/decoder halves, and DSpark adds draft + confidence-scheduled verification. Closest production reference for CAMOE's base architecture.
DeepSeek-V4 (Pro/Flash) preview: hybrid compressed attention, mHC residuals, Muon. Predecessor of V4.1-Flash; baseline architecture context.

DSpark: a drafter proposes several tokens, a confidence head predicts which will be accepted, verification length is scheduled. A draft-then-check mechanism inside a production model, but judged for speed/acceptance, not quality.
YOCO: decoder-decoder architecture that V4.1-Flash's Causal Encoder-Decoder is inspired by. Needed to understand where a whole-input representation exists in the stack.

Energy-Based Transformers: learn a verifier that scores (input, candidate prediction) compatibility from unsupervised pretraining alone, then refine the prediction by minimising that score. A learned internal critic that drives refinement; key reference for item 3 (critic training signal).

Large Concept Models: language modelling over whole-sentence embeddings (SONAR, 200 languages) instead of tokens. Precedent for a whole-sentence internal representation, the thing option (c) critiques.

Cola DLM: text -> continuous latent (VAE), global semantic prior via diffusion in latent space, then decode. Separates global meaning from surface wording; a possible substrate for a latent whole-sentence draft.
Recurrent-depth model (3.5B, 800B tokens) that iterates a block in latent space to scale test-time compute. Mechanism for 'another internal pass' without writing text.
Encode-Think-Decode: iterate only a subset of reasoning-relevant layers; includes adaptive per-token depth. Shows repasses can be added to an existing architecture.

Diagnoses learned halting gates in looped Transformers: simple confidence readouts often match learned gates; joint gate training distorts trajectories. Directly relevant to 'critic decides whether another pass is needed'.
Adaptive per-layer looping with learned halting plus gated memory banks; the combination beats an iso-FLOP baseline. The nearest structural analogue to 'repass + memory' found so far.
Looped transformers: a k-layer model looped L times nearly matches a kL-layer model on reasoning. Theory/evidence that repeated internal passes can substitute for depth.
Adaptive Computation Time (Graves): a network learns how many steps to take before emitting output. The original learned 'when to stop thinking' mechanism.
Coconut: reason in continuous hidden states instead of written chain-of-thought. Supports item 6's position that thinking need not be verbalised.

Latent planning emerges with scale (Qwen-3 0.6B-14B): models internally plan future words (e.g. 'an' before 'accountant'). Evidence on whether a whole-sentence plan exists inside ordinary models, and how to measure it.
Latent Refinement Decoding for diffusion LMs: keep uncertain positions as soft beliefs, refine with a feedback loop, stop by KL convergence. A whole-sequence refine-until-stable mechanism.
ProSeCo: masked diffusion model trained to correct its own already-generated tokens across the whole sequence. Shows a way to train correction from the model's own outputs.
Quality-aware decoding for NMT: use quality-estimation models to rerank/choose translations. External-critic baseline in output space (the option (b) family).
Token-level QE model that scores partial translations and is integrated into decoding. A critic that judges unfinished output; contrast point for option (c).
GEMBA-MQM: LLM marks translation error spans by MQM category without references. Possible tool for labelling Filipino translation errors (authors caution about using it to claim improvements).
AutoMQM: LLMs identify and categorise individual translation errors (MQM). Method for the Filipino error study and a possible critic training signal.
FilBench: Filipino, Tagalog and Cebuano benchmark over 27 LLMs; finds weaknesses in reading comprehension and translation. Starting point for which Filipino errors matter.
Kalahi: 150 handcrafted prompts by native speakers for Filipino cultural appropriateness. Covers register/culture errors a critic might target.
SEA-HELM: holistic Southeast Asian evaluation suite including linguistic pillars. Regional evaluation context for Filipino results.
Zooter: distil reward-model scores into a router that sends each query to the best LLM. Reward-guided routing at model level; reference for the RL critique router idea.

Patterns seen in latent-reasoning models' hidden states also appear in controls and don't always causally affect behaviour: treat latent thoughts as hidden computation, not hidden explanation. Caution for CAMOE's 'not black magic' claim: readability must be shown causally.

FRED difficulty metrics for low-resource MT. The abstract credits train-test overlap and pretraining exposure, but the paper's own regression (§3.3, Table 3) finds train-test similarity (R-score) explains most variation (R²=0.582) while pretraining exposure explains almost none (R²=0.0142). Guides contamination checks: check train-test overlap first. (Corrected 2026-09-24 after the A6 review.)

SONAR: 200-language fixed-size sentence embedding space built from a pretrained MT encoder-decoder with a single-vector bottleneck, trained with translation + MSE + denoising. Its weights are non-commercial, but this recipe is what DiaGrad would reimplement on a permissive base (ideas/03).

OmniSONAR: extends SONAR-style embeddings to thousands of language varieties via an LLM-initialised encoder-decoder plus teacher-student distillation. Method reference for scaling to more Philippine languages; no public weights found on HF (2026-09-24).

MADLAD-400: audited 400+ language web dataset and the Apache-2.0 MT models trained on it (11 Philippine languages on the model card). Proposed permissive starting point for DiaGrad's own sentence space (ideas/03, Path A).
vec2text: text can be largely reconstructed from embeddings by training an inverting decoder. Basis for Path C (permissive encoder + our own decoder). Repo has no license, so method only.

Gnosis: a lightweight module reads a frozen LLM's hidden states and attention patterns to predict its own failures, without external judges or text self-critique. The nearest found example of a critic that judges from internal states; CAMOE differs in making the critic a trained architectural component that triggers repasses (to verify).
Language models are largely calibrated about what they know (P(True), P(IK)). Foundation for the confidence baseline the critic must beat (DILIGENCE T1 #4).
Internal flow signatures: audits how a decision forms across depth, from internal dynamics, to self-check and refine. Another internal-state checker; possible source of critic input features.
Studies whether large reasoning models' visible self-critique actually detects inserted errors, and decodes the mechanism. Evidence for item 6 on how reliable text-based 'pseudo-critique' is.

Iterative translation refinement by prompting an LLM to self-correct, inspired by human translation; human evaluators found better fluency. Output-level (option b) baseline; also shows string metrics can drop while quality improves.
TACTIC: multi-agent translation built on cognitive translation studies. Grounding for item 6 (human multi-pass translation) and an output-level comparison point.

Embedding inversion via conditional masked diffusion: a 78M model recovers text from an embedding in 8 passes without access to the encoder. Cheap decoder option for Path C of the sentence-space substrate.
R3: MoE routing is unstable under RL because training and inference routers disagree; fix by replaying inference routing. Practical hazard for any RL-trained router or critic in an MoE.

AfriMTE/AfriCOMET: simplified MQM protocol for non-expert native speakers plus a COMET built on a regionally trained encoder. Template for a Philippine-language COMET and annotation protocol. (From A6 review.)
SSA-COMET: 14 African language pairs; chrF++ beat COMET-22 where the encoder lacks the language; LLM judges need few-shot examples and error-span prompting lowered correlation. (From A6 review.)
Zero-shot MT evaluation for four low-resource Indian languages: best learned metrics only reach Kendall tau ~0.32; GEMBA-MQM weaker. Calibrates expectations for metric reliability. (From A6 review.)

WMT24++: English->Filipino references and post-edits (Apache-2.0), ranked by automatic metrics only; authors say human evaluation is still needed. Only large public en-fil MT reference set found. (From A6 review.)

ESA human-evaluation protocol: cheaper than MQM with comparable quality; reports MQM same-annotator category+severity agreement of only 8.4%, which caps how accurately a critic's named categories can be scored. (From A6 review.)
Recommends comparing metric-human agreement with human-human agreement. Basis for DiaGrad's per-language metric-validation study. (From A6 review.)
Last Translation Benchmark: rule-verified hard translation cases including 36 Filipino items; model for a Philippine challenge set. (From A6 review.)
FLORES+ quality problems; named-entity copying inflates BLEU. Caution for using FLORES Philippine entries. (From A6 review.)

Batayan: Filipino/Taglish benchmark; re-translated FLORES Filipino to reduce translationese; evidence that MT over-uses ay-inversion. Source for Philippine-specific error categories. (From A6 review.)
UD-NewsCrawl Tagalog treebank: describes the Tagalog voice/focus system (ang/ng/sa marking) behind the proposed voice/focus error category. (From A6 review.)
XLM-R: its CC-100 language table (Filipino the only Philippine language) determines COMET-family metric coverage. (From A6 review.)
mT5: mC4 language table (fil, ceb) determines MetricX coverage; also the Path B substrate candidate. (From A6 review.)
COMET is blind to number and named-entity errors (found via MBR decoding). Failure mode to guard against. (From A6 review.)
Freitag et al.: MQM by professional translators outperforms crowd direct assessment; basis of modern MQM evaluation. (From A6 review.)
xCOMET: open span-level error metric (severity only); baseline for the critic's error spans. Weights are CC-BY-NC-SA: evaluation only, not a training signal. (From A6 review.)
Omnilingual MT: BLASER 3, Met-BOUQuET and the XSTS+R+P human protocol for long-tail languages; Philippine coverage unchecked. (From A6 review.)
NLLB: defines FLORES-200 and its hidden test split. Cited for benchmark provenance only; NLLB weights are non-commercial and must not generate training data. (From A5 review.)
FLORES-101: origin of spBLEU; Tagalog and Cebuano FLORES public since 2021, so exposure to web crawls is plausible. (From A5 review.)
Belebele: reading comprehension built on FLORES passages; a FLORES leak also leaks Belebele passages (not questions). Authors warn about crawl contamination. (From A5 review.)
Tatoeba Challenge: documents test-train overlap with OPUS. Reason Tatoeba Philippine pairs are diagnostics only. (From A5 review.)

Controlled study of MT contamination: leaking both source and reference inflated BLEU by up to 30 points at 8B scale; little effect for languages the model barely knows. Tagalog/Cebuano more exposed than smaller languages. (From A5 review.)
ConTAM: longest-match n-gram contamination detection with small n; method for DiaGrad's pre-evaluation check. (From A5 review.)
CONDA 2024 contamination database: lists FLORES inside xP3 and several models (BLOOMZ, mT0, Claude 3 Opus). (From A5 review.)
GPT-3: origin of the 13-gram overlap / clean-subset reporting convention. (From A5 review.)
BOUQuET: hand-written MT benchmark with hidden evaluation, including Tagalog. Lower contamination risk. (From A5 review.)
FineWeb2: multilingual pretraining corpus; its crawl window bounds which benchmarks it can contain. (From A5 review.)
CulturaX: multilingual corpus (mC4 + OSCAR); crawl window and license terms need checking (no license found at source by the audit). (From A5 review.)
HPLT v2: multilingual web corpus; crawl window for contamination reasoning. (From A5 review.)
DeepSeek-V3: V4 inherits its data preprocessing; closest statement of DeepSeek's data handling (still no decontamination detail for Philippine languages). (From A5 review.)
SEACrowd: catalogue of Southeast Asian and Philippine datasets; source for finding further evaluation and training sets. (From A5 review.)
Cultivar: evidence of FLORES overfitting. Caution against headline results on FLORES. (From A5 review.)
Sparsely-gated MoE: a trainable gating network (router) picks a few experts per example before they run. Defines the 'prior routing' that DiaGrad's posterior routing complements. (Search S40.)
Switch Transformer: top-1 expert routing with load balancing; standard reference for token-level routing at scale. (Search S42.)
DeepSeekMoE: fine-grained and shared experts; the router design used by DeepSeek-V3/V4/V4.1 that DiaGrad would build next to. (Search S39.)
PPO: standard policy-gradient algorithm; candidate for training the critique router (D5). (Search S38.)
DeepSeekMath: introduces GRPO (group-relative policy optimisation, no value network); candidate for training the critique router (D5). (Search S41.)
Mixture-of-Recursions: a learned router decides per-token recursion depth; closest analogue of REPASS as learned adaptive computation (pre-circulation review M4; D7).
AutoMix: self-verification of a small model's written answer decides whether to escalate to a larger model; posterior routing between whole models over written output (review M4; D7).
FrugalGPT: LLM cascade with a learned scorer deciding whether to accept an answer or call a stronger model; posterior routing between models over written output (review M4; D7).
gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b model card: decoder-only MoE that Sapin-sapin AI continued-pretrained; candidate later target for porting posterior routing (review O1; D7). Licence to be audited.

Deliberation Networks (NIPS 2017): a first-pass decoder writes a raw sequence and a second-pass decoder polishes it, the classic two-pass 'think twice' MT design. The first pass is decoded text and every sentence gets the second pass; no critic decides and no experts are routed. Not on arXiv; added after review M4 (2026-09-24).

MetricX-24 (WMT 2024 metrics task): the learned MT metric used as the critique router's reward Q in the first prototype (D7/D8); Apache-2.0 per our licence audit; excluded from the evidence because it trains the router.
Transformer (Attention Is All You Need): attention, FFN, encoder-decoder; foundation chapter. S74 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
T5: encoder-decoder text-to-text transformer; base family of mT5/MADLAD. S70 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Chinchilla: compute-optimal training; FLOP accounting context. S72 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Bengio et al.: straight-through estimator and conditional computation; gradients through discrete choices. S71 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Eigen et al.: deep (stacked) mixture of experts; step from 1991 MoE to deep nets. S55/S59 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
GShard: first very large MoE Transformer, for multilingual MT; top-2 gating, capacity, auxiliary loss. S46 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
ST-MoE: training instability and router z-loss; what experts specialise in. S47 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Expert-choice routing: experts pick tokens; variable compute per token. S48 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Hash layers: routing by hashing with no learned router; baseline for 'does the router matter'. S49 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
BASE layers: routing as balanced linear assignment. S50 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Soft MoE: experts process weighted mixtures of tokens. S51 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Auxiliary-loss-free load balancing via per-expert bias (used by DeepSeek-V3). S52 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Sparse upcycling: MoE initialised from a dense checkpoint; relevant to our encoder MoE. S53 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
MegaBlocks: dropless MoE training with block-sparse kernels; systems chapter. S54 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Mixtral: open sparse MoE, 8 experts top-2; routing analysis. S55 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
OLMoE: fully open MoE with specialisation analysis. S56 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Scaling laws for fine-grained MoE (granularity). S57 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Unified scaling laws for routed language models. S58 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
A Survey on Mixture of Experts: overview for the explainer. S73 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Demons in the Detail: implementing the load-balancing loss and its effect on expert specialisation (2025). S52/S62 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Statistical benefits of shared experts and normalised sigmoid gating in DeepSeekMoE (2025). S45 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Three phases of expert routing during MoE training (2026). S45/S59/S60 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
The Illusion of Specialization: domain-invariant 'standing committee' of experts (2026). S45/S59/S61 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Equifinality: routing topology does not determine LM quality (2026). S45/S60 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Multilingual Routing in Mixture-of-Experts (2025): how MoE routes across languages. S60 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Scaling laws for efficient MoE language models (2025). S57 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Advancing Expert Specialization for Better MoE (2025). S61/S62 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Super Experts in MoE LLMs (2025): a few experts matter disproportionately; relevant to rerouting away from hub experts. S61/S73 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Coupling experts and routers via an auxiliary loss (2025). S60 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Fixing MoE over-fitting on low-resource languages in multilingual MT. S63 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Survey of dynamic model routing and cascading (2026): context for posterior routing between models. S73 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Universal Transformers: recurrent depth with adaptive computation. S66 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
PonderNet: learned probabilistic halting. S65 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Mixture-of-Depths: routing tokens around blocks to allocate compute. S64 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
CALM: confidence-based early exit per token. S67 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Reward model overoptimisation scaling laws (Goodhart evidence). S68 (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
DeepSeek-V2: MLA and DeepSeekMoE at scale; lineage between DeepSeekMoE and V3. (DeepSeek lineage; direct ID) (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan, Hinton 1991: Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts, the origin of MoE (gating network + experts). No open PDF: abstract only. (explainer extension 2026-09-24)
Jordan and Jacobs 1994: hierarchical mixtures of experts trained with EM. No open PDF: abstract only. (explainer extension 2026-09-24)

Williams 1992: REINFORCE, the basic policy-gradient estimator with a baseline; foundation for the router's RL. Springer's PDF link returns a web page to scripts and OpenAlex has no abstract, so this record is metadata only: cite for attribution, and check claims via papers that describe REINFORCE. (explainer extension 2026-09-24)

R2-T2: re-routing in test-time for multimodal MoE. Moves a test sample's routing weights towards those of correctly answered neighbours; no base-model training. Nearest prior on re-routing experts at inference; differs from DiaGrad: the signal is neighbour success, not a critic judging the model's own draft, and there is no learned accept/redo policy. (prior-work audit r3, S75/S77/S83, D10, 2026-10-02)

C3PO: test-time expert re-mixing in critical layers and core experts, optimising a surrogate from successful reference neighbours; reports a 10-20% accuracy gap left by pretrained expert selection. Supports DiaGrad's motivation; differs as R2-T2 does. (prior-work audit r3, S75/S77/S83, D10, 2026-10-02)

Dynamic Experts Search: varies the number of active experts at test time to diversify reasoning paths and selects with a verifier. Verifier plus expert-space variation, but over written outputs and without critique-directed rerouting. (prior-work audit r3, S75/S77/S83, D10, 2026-10-02)

Counterfactual Routing (ACL 2026): training-free inference that shifts expert activation towards causally important 'dormant' experts at a constant activation count. Rerouting at equal compute, without a critic. (prior-work audit r3, S75/S77/S83, D10, 2026-10-02)

ESRL: expert-space exploration in MoE RL. Finds that perturbing routing alters outputs much like raising decoding temperature. Motivates DiaGrad's random-direction reroute baseline: a REROUTE gain could come from diversity alone. (prior-work audit r3, S75/S77/S83, D10, 2026-10-02)

Statistical power in NLP: underpowered comparisons are common; small test sets and typical human-rating designs often cannot detect small model differences, inflating claimed gains. Sizes DiaGrad's D5 and human-eval designs before claiming a REROUTE gain.

Quantifies benchmark variance (seed variance across initialisations, monotonicity during training) and gives recommendations. A difference smaller than the seed variance it measures is not a result; informs how many seeds tranche-1 needs.

How many random seeds: links seed count to error rates for t-test and bootstrap comparisons of two algorithms, and shows violated test assumptions distort them. Seeds cost compute (item 4) and set what a comparison can detect (item 7).
Argues for bootstrap confidence intervals on the difference between systems instead of SOTA status or bare significance tests. Reporting format for CAMOE vs baselines.
Adaptive data analysis: choosing analyses after seeing holdout results breaks standard inference and false-discovery control. Why D5 is read once and the prereg fixes analyses before tranche-1 data.

Provable black-box contamination test: a contaminated model finds a benchmark's canonical example order much likelier than shuffled orders. Usable on public Filipino sets (FLORES, Belebele) as part of the A5 audit.
Contamination is forgotten only when training runs far past Chinchilla-scale tokens; at Chinchilla scale even minor contamination overfits. Small fine-tuning runs cannot assume leaked items wash out.

Preference leakage: LLM judges favour outputs from the model, family or descendant that generated the training data. Another reason an LLM judge is not evidence and a critic trained on one model's data is suspect.
CALM: quantifies 12 biases of LLM-as-a-judge; significant biases persist in specific tasks. Supports human evaluation as primary evidence and caution with LLM critics as label sources.

Reward models are underspecified: optimising against one does not raise reward under another trained on the same data; ensembles mitigate but do not eliminate reward hacking. Relevant to RL reward Q for the critique router and the metric-as-evidence rule.

Iterative self-refinement with a same-model evaluator drifts from human judgment: evaluator ratings rise while quality stagnates (reward hacking). Direct risk for a critic sharing weights with workers; human eval is the check.

LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning without external feedback and sometimes get worse. Item 6 contrast: visible intrinsic self-critique fails, so CAMOE's critic must add information the worker lacks; REPASS-without-critic is the baseline.

Small (<=13B) LMs self-correct reasoning mainly when paired with a strong verifier; training on critiques of their own errors helps. Bears on critic strength vs worker strength and where critic labels come from.

Tokenizers encode the same text at very different lengths across languages (up to 15x). Token budgets, context limits and per-token compute are not comparable across Philippine languages; compare in words or characters.
Off-target (wrong-language) translation rises when languages' vocabularies are lexically close. Closely related Philippine languages need language-ID checks before chrF++ credit.

Fine-tuning an aligned model can erode its safety behaviour, even without malicious data. Post-training side effects appear on behaviours the held-out set does not cover; mainly OpenGrad-relevant, kept for any DiaGrad fine-tune of an aligned base.

SimSiam: one encoder shared by two branches with a stop-gradient on one; the shared encoder still trains through the other branch. Cited in the maths guide to explain what detaching the first draft does and does not do (D13, 2026-10-04).

Back-translation at scale. Sampling beats beam except in the 80K low-resource setting, where beam wins. Basis for the back-translation generation setting (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)

Tagged back-translation: one tag token matches or beats noising. Basis for tagging every synthetic slice (U3) (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)

Human evaluation shows back-translation helps natural-source text too, and BLEU misses it. Argues for human evaluation on natural-source sets (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)
Sequence-level knowledge distillation: train on teacher translations (bigger-teacher re-translation) (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)

Multilingual knowledge distillation of sentence embeddings (MSE to a teacher); Tagalog Tatoeba 86.2/84.0 from 36k pairs (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)
LASER3 teacher-student encoders plus MLM and curriculum; the miner behind our NLLB en-tl pairs (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)

SMOL: our D19 gate test set, and the post-editing precedent (Gemini drafts, about 70% of sentences changed) (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)
Forward-translated synthetic data with human ratings; Bicleaner-AI weakly correlated with humans (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)

TopXGen: LLM-written low-resource text back-translated with NLLB-3.3B; example for the NLLB-output question (D25) (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)
Aya Collection: translated with NLLB-3.3B and released Apache-2.0; licence-practice example for D25 (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)

Polyglot Teachers: which teacher model to use for synthetic data; Tagalog case study (D25 teacher comparison) (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)
Augmentation direction should follow the resource gradient (back-translate the low-resource side) (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)
NewsPaLM: LLM-generated MBR/QE-selected data beats 300x larger web data (en-de) (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)
Morphology-aware dictionary augmentation (Taglish / lexicon augmentation) (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)
CCMatrix: margin-based bitext mining at web scale; one of our D22 corpora (2026-10-17 techniques survey, research/data-survey/data-gathering-techniques-2026-10-17.md)

Quality Does Matter: top-ranked slices of web-mined corpora (incl. NLLB) beat random or bottom slices; NLLB top is religious-heavy. Evidence for D22 filtering (2026-10-17 corpus survey, research/notes/final_report_en-fil-parallel-corpora-f90c6f.md)

Separating Grains from the Chaff: strict classifier filtering of mined data wins for African languages (WMT22). Evidence for D22 filtering (2026-10-17 corpus survey, research/notes/final_report_en-fil-parallel-corpora-f90c6f.md)
NusaMT-7B: LASER3 floor 1.09, GlotLID 0.9 and OpusFilter heuristics for mined data; our rank 5M sits at 1.09 (2026-10-17 corpus survey, research/notes/final_report_en-fil-parallel-corpora-f90c6f.md)

BitextEdit: keeping the 1.05-1.06 CCMatrix band helped when data was scarce; the counter-evidence to hard filtering (2026-10-17 corpus survey, research/notes/final_report_en-fil-parallel-corpora-f90c6f.md)

A Shocking Amount of the Web is Machine Translated: LASER favours MT output; multi-way-parallel text is mostly MT. Explains MT-heavy top of NLLB en-tl (2026-10-17 corpus survey, research/notes/final_report_en-fil-parallel-corpora-f90c6f.md)

Quality at a Glance: audit of web-crawled corpora; CCAligned en-tl 13% correct. Basis for excluding CCAligned (D22) (2026-10-17 corpus survey, research/notes/final_report_en-fil-parallel-corpora-f90c6f.md)

IndicTrans2: LaBSE >= 0.80 re-filter of allenai/nllb dropped 76% and gained chrF++. Basis for the second-opinion filter (D22) (2026-10-17 corpus survey, research/notes/final_report_en-fil-parallel-corpora-f90c6f.md)
HPLT 3.0: bilingual data for 28 European languages only; no Tagalog pairs (D22 screening) (2026-10-17 corpus survey, research/notes/final_report_en-fil-parallel-corpora-f90c6f.md)
HPLT v1: 18 English-paired languages, no Tagalog (D22 screening) (2026-10-17 corpus survey, research/notes/final_report_en-fil-parallel-corpora-f90c6f.md)
